zoom_levels_observed: BEAST-WIDE: head+torso+chair, face centre ~30% of frame height, head spans ~32% H (shots 1, 3, 11)
BEAST-TIGHT: ~1.5x punch of the same camera, face centre ~33%, head spans ~52% H (shots 4, 6, 8, 10)
RUG-CLEAN: single fixed crop of the second caller's cam, face centre ~55% H (shots 5, 7, 9) - provably one identical crop
RUG-STREAMPAGE: the raw stream layout incl. his burned-in 'SUBS: 5285/7...' bar and a photo panel (shot 2 only)
framing_style.description: Two-caller phone-call edit assembled from two separate stream feeds. There is NO animated camera move inside any shot: every one of the 11 shots is a pixel-static crop. Verified by using the burned-in caption as a rigid transform probe - its vertical centre holds to within +/-0.2% of frame height for the whole of shots 3,4,6,8,10 (e.g. 77.81% constant, spread 0.00-0.41%), and by ORB/RANSAC background alignment head-vs-tail returning scale 1.000, dx 0.0, dy 0.0 with 400-1300 inliers on shots 5,7,8,9,11 and shot-4-tail vs shot-6-head (scale 1.000, dx 0.2, dy -0.1, 331 inliers). All 'movement' is therefore done by CUTTING between fixed crops, not by keyframed zoom. 8 of 10 cuts swap between the two callers' feeds; only 2 of 10 (t=3.75 wide->tight, t=24.017 tight->wide) reframe the same camera, hence same_scene_reframe_pct = 20. The single exception to the static rule is the opening: 0.0-0.55s is a centre-anchored full-frame scale ramp from roughly 1.8x down to 1.0x (measured via caption cap-height: 1.58x at t=0.14, 1.45x at 0.18, 1.32x at 0.22, 1.15x at 0.30, 1.12x at 0.40, 1.00x by 0.55s), and it scales the burned-in captions along with the picture - i.e. it is applied to the finished composite, not to the video layer alone. Subject is NOT face-tracked or centred: MrBeast's face sits high (~30% of frame height), Rug's sits low (~55%), because each is just a fixed crop of a different source stream layout.

caption.position: horizontally centred (cx = 50.0% of width); vertical centre locked at 77.9% of frame height for 9 of the 11 shots, with a measured spread under 0.5% within each shot. Two deliberate exceptions: 72.3% through the opening shot (0.7-2.4s) and 62.1% during shot 2, where it is nudged up to clear the streamer's own burned-in 'SUBS' bar.
caption.style_description: Heavy condensed all-caps grotesque (Anton / Impact-like), cap height ~130 px = ~6.8% of frame height. One to three words per card, overwhelmingly one or two. 77 cards over 27.4s = ~169 cards/min, mean 0.36s on screen (card gaps p10/p50/p90 = 0.15/0.30/0.65s). Captions run continuously - present in 273 of 274 sampled frames. THE COLOUR IS KEYED TO WHO IS SPEAKING, NOT TO WHAT IS ON SCREEN: cyan = MrBeast, yellow = Rug. The two normally coincide because the edit cuts to whoever is talking, but the window 23.5-24.0s shows MrBeast on screen with a YELLOW card ('LETS GO!') because Rug is the one speaking off-camera - that is the decisive case and it proves the mapping is speaker->colour.
caption.color: cyan #00FFFF (MrBeast) / yellow #FFFF00 (Rug) - both measured as pure primaries from modal pixel values (#00F8F8 and #F8F800 at 8-level quantisation)
caption.outline: solid black outline ~22 px at 1080x1920 (~17% of cap height), symmetric on all four sides, with slightly rounded corner joins; plus a soft low-opacity black drop shadow offset a further ~6-10 px down and right
caption.animation: no per-word karaoke highlight and no visible pop/scale entry on individual cards - cards hard-swap at full size. The only scaling seen on captions is the opening 0-0.55s full-frame zoom-out ramp, which scales them because it is applied to the finished composite.

effects: opening full-frame zoom-out: ~1.8x -> 1.0x over ~0.55s, centre-anchored, applied over the burned-in captions
circular profile-photo sticker of the second caller (Rug) with a white ring, ~0.4s at t=1.35-1.75s, popped in over MrBeast's chest exactly on the caption card 'RUG'
speaker-coded caption colour (cyan MrBeast / yellow Rug) used as the only 'who is talking' device
hard cuts only - no transitions of any kind

burned-in source-stream graphics inherited from the recordings, NOT added by the editor: top donation/donor ticker present throughout, red 'NEW SUBSCRIBER' banners on Rug's feed, and a 'RAISED $4,448,543.89' goal banner that appears near the end
hook: Opens cold, mid-sentence, on an extreme close-up of MrBeast's face at roughly 1.8x, which eases out to the wide framing over the first ~0.55s; captions are already running by the second frame ('I KEEP' -> 'SEEING' -> 'PEOPLE' -> 'CHAT' -> 'SAY' -> 'CALL' -> 'RUG' -> 'ILL'). At ~1.35-1.75s a circular photo of Rug pops in over MrBeast's chest on the word 'RUG'. There is no title card, no question overlay, no black frame and no establishing shot - the first frame is already a talking face at maximum zoom. First cut does not arrive until 2.40s, so the hook is carried entirely by the zoom-out plus the caption pace.
audio: Integrated -14.5 LUFS, LRA 1.7 LU, true peak -0.2 dBFS (Opus 48 kHz stereo source). The 1.7 LU loudness range is extremely narrow - heavy compression/limiting, loudness-maximised for feed playback. NO music bed: per-0.2s band energies swing 20-24 dB in every band including 20-120 Hz, which rules out a sustained musical floor. NO SFX hits on cuts: mean level rise at the 10 cut points is 11.5 dB versus 6.9 dB (sd 4.9) at 129 random non-cut times - only about 0.9 sd, consistent with cuts being placed on speech onsets rather than with added whooshes or impacts. Audio is therefore the raw two-way call/stream audio of the two speakers, normalised and limited. Never reaches digital silence; quietest 50 ms window is -45.6 dBFS.
notes:
COMPLETE. Every number here comes from a measurement or from frames actually viewed. Reproduction recipe in one line: crop two fixed 9:16 windows out of two source streams (a wide and a ~1.5x tight window on caller A, one fixed window on caller B), hard-cut between them on speech onsets at ~22 cuts/min, burn 1-2 word all-caps cards at 78% frame height in pure cyan or pure yellow chosen by WHO IS SPEAKING, and apply a single centre-anchored 1.8x->1.0x scale ramp over the first 0.55s of the finished composite.

METHOD NOTES: Scene detection at threshold 0.20 and 0.35 give identical hit lists (10 hits) and match what is visible in the cut-pair sheets, so 0.20 was used. Threshold 0.10 adds six extra hits (2.083, 2.183, 6.417, 11.85, 15.067, 26.35) that are NOT picture changes - they are caption cards swapping, exactly as warned. No collapsing was needed: the closest pair of real cuts is 0.667s apart. Frame-mean-luma analysis independently confirms 8 of the 10 cuts as single-frame steps of 38-53 luma (no dissolves anywhere, no white flash - zero frames above 200 luma, zero below 25); the two cuts it misses (3.75 and 24.017) are precisely the two same-camera reframes, which is a nice cross-check on the 20% reframe figure.

COULD NOT DETERMINE: (1) Exact font name - it is a heavy condensed grotesque consistent with Anton or Impact, but that cannot be verified from pixels alone. (2) The starting magnitude of the opening zoom - the caption is clipped off the bottom of frame before t=0.14, so 1.8x is extrapolated from the measured 1.58x at t=0.14; the easing curve was not fitted. (3) Face positions are approximate: this OpenCV build (5.0.0 headless) has no objdetect module and therefore no face detector, so face positions were read off a contact sheet ruled with 10% gridlines rather than measured. (4) speed_ramp_used=false is an inference, not a direct frame-timing test - it rests on the audio being continuous natural speech with no pitch or tempo artefacts and on every shot being a static crop. (5) ORB reported a consistent ~520-560 px horizontal offset at scale 1.0 between the BEAST-WIDE and BEAST-TIGHT groups; this is a false match caused by the repeating horizontal ticker bars across the top of the frame. It was rejected. The real relationship between those two crops is a scale change of roughly 1.5x, established from direct subject measurement (hair/face blob height 31-39% of frame height in the wide group versus 51-55% in the tight group) and confirmed visually on the gridded framing sheet. (6) words_per_card = 1.4 is the mean over the 46 cards legible on the contact sheets, not over all 77 detected cards.

EFFECTS EXPLICITLY CHECKED FOR AND ABSENT: white flash on hit, dissolves/fades, zoom lines, speed ramps, camera shake, pan/drift, meme cutaway, b-roll, arrows or circles, emoji stickers (the only sticker is the one circular avatar), added borders or letterboxing, film grain, vignette, chromatic aberration, and a progress bar (the bar visible at the end is the stream's own donation-goal banner, present only near the end, not an editor-added progress indicator).
